column1: This conclusion is not lost on policymakers. Those trying to pull the world’s poorest nations out of poverty, such as the advisers sent to developing nations by the World Bank, often advocate reducing fertility by increasing education about birth-control methods and expanding women’s job opportunities. Toward the same end, China has followed the totalitarian policy of allowing only one child for most urban couples (though in 2013 China started to relax the rule). These policies to reduce population growth should, if the Solow model is right, raise income per person in the long run.
